gap: No result ChatGPT got names an independent tester who ran a dual-monitor DisplayPort KVM. The only named test of a candidate is old: Igor'sLAB (Xaver Amberger, 2 Mar 2021) ran the Level1Techs DP 1.4 dual-monitor KVM at 1440p 144 Hz and 2160p 60 Hz 'without problems' with G-Sync working, and reported no added input lag but gave no figure.
standout_why: I compared against the TESmart pages ChatGPT got (the cited dks202-m24 page returned HTTP 429 twice, so I couldn't read it), dockgearhq.com/blog/best-kvm-switches-for-dual-monitor-setups-2026 and gearexplained.com/guides/dual-monitor-kvm-switch. Dockgearhq gives 'roughly 2–3 seconds' switching for the KD-E10 and iDock C20 with no source, calls the iDock figure a 'reported target', and treats the Level1Techs 1440p240 trouble as owner reports. Gearexplained says 'GearExplained did not test these products.' None of them names a tester or gives a measured figure for a dual-DP KVM. The Igor'sLAB run is the only named test, but it is from 2021, has no numbers, and covers only one candidate. No named lab has measured the TESmart DKS202-M24, the CKL, the ATEN CS1942DP(A) or the StarTech DP 1.4 unit.
decides: This doesn't change the pick. It only backs the Level1Techs unit at 1440p144 and 4K60 with adaptive sync, as seen by one named reviewer. Since no named lab has measured switching time, input lag or tested refresh for the TESmart DKS202-M24, the CKL or the StarTech, any ranking among them rests on maker specs. Write it that way rather than claiming 'tested' performance. The page can still say plainly that the Level1Techs store listing states it 'does not support monitor emulation', so the monitors re-handshake and windows may shuffle on every switch.
